text: Mercury has slowed to a crawl and is about to turn backward, which it does three times a year for about three weeks at a stretch. The week around the turn is the odd one. A planet at its station is a planet concentrated, and Mercury rules the traffic of your daily life: messages, plans, travel, paperwork, the small machinery that moves your information around. Around this turn that machinery gets glitchy. Emails cross, appointments slide, a device picks this week to act up, and conversations you thought were settled reopen. None of it is punishment. Mercury turning backward opens a review stretch, and the friction is the invitation. Something from the recent past, a decision made quickly, a message sent in haste, a project pushed out before it was ready, wants a second look. You tend to do your best work now by finishing rather than launching: rereading before sending, confirming what you assumed was confirmed, backing up what you would hate to lose. Old threads resurface too. A person you had not thought about, an idea you shelved, a plan you abandoned can come back around, and some of them deserve the second chance. The next three weeks reward revision more than speed, so drafts, edits, and reconsiderations go well even while launches wobble. You get the most from this turn by dropping the assumption that forward is the only useful direction. Thinking has a backstitch in it, and this is the week the needle turns.

The review is ending. Mercury has spent about three weeks moving backward, and this week it stands still and swings forward again. Oddly, the station itself is often the bumpiest part of the whole stretch: a planet changing direction sits at maximum pause, so the crossed wires and stalled plans of the past weeks can peak in your life right as they begin to clear. Give the fog a little room to lift. Clarity comes back in layers over the following days rather than all at once. What the turn marks is release. Conversations that stalled find their footing, delayed answers arrive, and decisions you kept reopening finally consent to stay closed. If you spent the backward stretch revising, the value shows now: the edited draft reads better than the rushed one would have, and the reconsidered plan holds. Momentum builds gradually, and the projects and messages that waited start to move again, usually the oldest first. This is also the natural moment to act on what the review taught you. Whatever you noticed about your habit of hasty replies or unchecked assumptions is easiest to change while the lesson is fresh. Mercury makes this turn several times a year, so nothing here is rare or dire; it is the sky's regular rhythm of draft and revision. This week the marked-up pages come back, and the weeks ahead are for the clean copy.

Venus stands still this week and begins to move backward, something it does only every year and a half or so, for about six weeks at a time. Of all the planetary turns this one reaches furthest into the personal, because Venus carries what you love, what you find beautiful, and what you feel you are worth. When it pauses, those questions pause with it and turn inward. The weeks ahead tend to run on reassessment. Relationships come up for quiet review, not necessarily in crisis, but in questions: is this still nourishing, is this what I want, was I fair to that person years ago. Old loves have a way of reappearing during a backward Venus, in person, in dreams, or in a name you suddenly cannot stop thinking about, and the visit is usually about finishing something rather than restarting it. Taste goes strange too. What looked right last month can look wrong now, which is why big aesthetic commitments made this week, the haircut, the purchase, the redecoration, often read differently once Venus moves on. Money and worth sit in the same basket: your spending habits and the price you put on your own effort both come under the lamp. None of this asks for action yet. The station week simply opens the file. You work with it best by letting attraction and doubt both count as information, noticing what resurfaces, and saving verdicts for when Venus is moving forward again and you can see what the review actually found.

After about six weeks of backward motion, Venus is standing still and turning forward. The long review of your affections, taste, and worth is closing, and the station week is where its findings surface. Feelings that were tangled begin to state themselves plainly. You often discover you already know the answer to the question the retrograde asked: whether the relationship gets another chapter, whether the old flame was a door or an echo, whether the thing you wanted was the thing itself or just its packaging. What this turn marks is settling. Connections that survived the reassessment tend to move forward on firmer ground, sometimes with a warmth that feels new because it is chosen rather than assumed. Whatever ended during the backward weeks starts to feel finished instead of raw. Desire comes back to the present tense: your eye for what pleases you steadies, and commitments made from here on tend to hold up better than the ones from the review stretch. Worth is the quietest gain. Many people come out of a Venus retrograde asking a little more for their work and tolerating a little less in their company, and the direct station is when that shift takes hold in you. The pace of the heart picks back up slowly over the following days. You do not have to force conclusions this week; mostly you get to keep the ones the review already reached.

Mars grinds to a halt this week, and when Mars stops, you feel the brakes. This turn comes around only every two years or so and opens a backward stretch of roughly ten weeks. Mars is drive: the push behind your ambition, anger, desire, and getting things done. At its station that push has nowhere to go, so the week can feel like flooring the pedal in neutral. Efforts that were sailing hit resistance, projects stall for reasons no one can quite name, and tempers run shorter because frustration has fewer outlets. The temptation is to push harder. It usually backfires; force applied at a Mars station tends to bounce. What the turn actually marks is the start of a strategic review. For the next couple of months the question is not how hard you are pushing but whether you are pushing at the right thing. Desire gets audited: ambitions you inherited rather than chose, fights you keep having on autopilot, goals that stopped meaning anything a while ago all come up for inspection. Your energy runs lower or strangely uneven during this stretch, and old angers can resurface asking to be understood instead of re-fought. The gains go to whoever treats the slowdown as reconnaissance. Sharpen the plan, train instead of race, and let the stalled push tell you where the aim was off. When Mars turns forward again you get the horsepower back, and it goes furthest behind an aim the review has corrected.

The engine catches again. Mars has spent around ten weeks moving backward, a slow-burn stretch that arrives only once every couple of years, and this week it stops dead and turns forward. Stations concentrate a planet's nature, so the days around the turn can feel combustible: energy that pooled in you during the retrograde wants out, and it is not always graceful about the exit. Short fuses, sudden urges to act, and a restless revving quality are common right at the turn. The release is real, though. What this station marks is the return of traction. Projects that stalled for no visible reason start responding again, your physical energy climbs back toward normal, and the ambition that went quiet begins to state its demands. The best of it belongs to what the backward weeks taught you. If the retrograde showed you a goal that no longer fit, a fight not worth having, or a smarter route to the same summit, this is when acting on that knowledge becomes possible and satisfying. Momentum rebuilds over days and weeks rather than hours, and the first moves out of a Mars station reward deliberateness; the reckless ones tend to leave marks. Anger you examined during the retrograde can now be spent cleanly, as a boundary or a decision instead of a smolder. Two years of forward Mars open from here, and the direction you point it this week counts for more than the speed.

Once a year Jupiter slows, stands still, and spends about four months moving backward, and this week is the turn. Jupiter is the growth principle: your confidence, opportunity, belief, the sense that more is possible. Its station does not usually bring the sky down; the shift is quieter than a Mercury or Mars turn, more a change of weather than an event. Outward expansion loses a little steam. Your plans for bigger things, the new venture, the next horizon, the leap of faith, tend to slow or reveal a soft spot around now, and the invitation is to grow inward instead. The backward months favor questions of belief: whether the philosophy you run on still describes the world you actually live in, whether the goals you are chasing would satisfy you if you caught them, whether your optimism is faith or habit. Studies, teachings, and books you meant to return to reward attention now. Luck does not vanish during a backward Jupiter; it relocates, showing up more through what you revisit than what you launch. An opportunity from the past can circle back looking different. You get the most from this turn by letting scale rest for a season and asking what the growth was for. Expansion that survives that question tends to be the kind that lasts, and Jupiter will be moving forward again in time to build on it.

Jupiter's yearly backward stretch is ending. After roughly four months of retreat it hangs motionless this week and turns forward, and what has been ripening quietly in you starts looking for room. This tends to be one of the friendlier stations. Confidence that thinned during the backward months begins refilling, doors that would not budge loosen, and plans you shelved at the start of the review suddenly seem worth taking down again. The growth that resumes now has usually changed shape. Months of reconsidering what you believe and what you are aiming for leave a mark, and the ambitions that survive a Jupiter retrograde tend to be fewer and truer than the ones that went in. This week marks the handoff from understanding to expansion. Opportunities begin arriving from outside again rather than from the archive, and saying yes starts to feel like the natural answer instead of a gamble. The scale of things can shift quickly once Jupiter moves, so the weeks after the turn often carry a growth spurt: an offer, an opening, an audience, a green light. The old caution about Jupiter still applies, since more is not always better and the planet enlarges whatever it touches, wisdom and excess alike. But the season favors reach. What you studied, questioned, and quietly outgrew during the backward months is your platform, and the forward months are for building on it.

Saturn comes to a standstill this week and begins about four and a half months of backward motion, a turn it makes once a year. Saturn is structure: your commitments, duties, ambitions with deadlines, the load-bearing walls of your life. When it stations, the weight of all that becomes briefly hard to ignore. The week around the turn often lands as a heaviness or a sobering, a sense that something you are responsible for is asking to be taken seriously. What opens is an audit. The backward months review the structures you have built and the obligations you have accepted: which commitments still deserve you, which rules you follow out of fear rather than sense, where the foundation was poured too fast. Progress on long-term goals tends to go internal during this stretch. The visible milestones slow while the real work shifts to inspection, reinforcement, and honest accounting. Authority themes come up for review too, both the authorities over you and your own way of carrying responsibility. None of this is punishment, though Saturn's turns rarely feel festive. A structure examined now can be repaired now, and the problems this review surfaces are almost always cheaper to fix during the backward months than after them. You work with the season by cooperating with the inspection: keeping promises small and real, shoring up what wobbles, and setting down loads that were never yours. What passes this audit tends to stand for years.

After some four and a half months of moving backward, Saturn halts this week and resumes forward motion. The long structural review is over, and the station marks the moment its conclusions start coming due. Saturn's direct turn tends to feel less like relief than like a report card arriving, though often a fair one. Matters of duty, career, and commitment that hung suspended through the backward months begin to resolve for you, and the resolutions usually match the work: what you reinforced holds, what you neglected asks its price, what you honestly released stops costing you. Doors that were stuck can open now precisely because the frame was rebuilt. The forward months favor construction. Plans that had to wait can be executed, responsibilities taken on now tend to stick, and efforts begun in the weeks after the turn often carry unusual staying power because they rest on inspected ground. There is frequently a maturity dividend as well. People come out of a Saturn retrograde clearer about what they can carry and what they will no longer apologize for, and the direct station is when that clarity becomes policy in your life. The pace stays Saturnine, which is to say slow and cumulative; nothing about this turn is sudden. But the drag of the review lifts, effort starts converting into results again, and the discipline you practiced in the backward stretch begins to pay its quiet compound interest.

This week Uranus stands still against the stars, then begins the backward drift it holds for about five months of every year. The whole world shares every Uranus station, so this is background weather rather than a personal summons, felt most when the slowed planet sits close to something in your own chart. Still, the turn has a signature. Uranus is the impulse to break pattern: the restlessness under your routines, the urge toward freedom, the sudden move. When it stations retrograde, that impulse turns inward and the revolution goes underground. The months ahead tend to review your relationship with change itself. Places where you have been performing rebellion without actually changing anything, and places where you have been performing stability while quietly suffocating, both become easier to see from inside. Restlessness during this stretch often shows up as a low internal hum rather than outer disruption: the job, the town, the arrangement still function, but some part of you has begun drafting the alternative. The station week can pop a surprise loose, since a planet at maximum pause is a planet at maximum voltage, but the deeper work is the slow one. Breakthroughs conceived now tend to surface months later, when Uranus turns forward. You use the season well by letting the misfit feelings speak without immediately obeying them, and by noticing which of your defiances are real.

Uranus finishes its yearly five-month backward stretch this week, pausing motionless before it swings ahead. Like all outer-planet turns it belongs to everyone at once, and it registers personally mainly when it lands near a sensitive spot in your chart. Its meaning, though, is distinctive: release of stored change. Through the backward months the urge for freedom and reinvention has been running as an inner current in you, rehearsing exits and redesigns without staging them. The direct station opens the door. In the weeks around and after the turn, changes that were only thoughts have a way of becoming events, in your life or in the surrounding world: the resignation actually tendered, the move actually booked, the truth actually said. There can be a static-electric feel to the station itself, a jumpiness, sudden news, plans reversing overnight, technology and schedules briefly haywire. The disruptions usually point in the direction things need to go. What this turn rewards is honesty about the alternative you have been drafting. If the backward months showed you where the life no longer fits the person, the forward ones supply the nerve and the opening. Not every impulse deserves obedience, and the ones that survive a night's sleep deserve your attention. Freedom taken deliberately now tends to cost less than freedom that has to erupt later.

Neptune's turn this week is the sky's quietest: the planet stops, then spends around five months of the year sliding backward, as it does annually. Everyone alive shares the station, so it works like a tide rather than a knock at your door, strongest where it touches your chart closely. Neptune governs the dissolving side of life: imagination, longing, faith, the dreams that keep you going, and the fog that keeps you from seeing. When it turns retrograde, the fog thins from the inside. The backward months tend to x-ray your ideals. Illusions you have been maintaining, about a person, a hope, a version of yourself, become gradually harder to sustain, not through disaster but through a slow leak of enchantment. This can feel like disappointment, and sometimes it is grief, but what it leaves behind is usually truer than what it takes. Dreams worth keeping survive the review and come out cleaner. Your creative and spiritual life often deepens now, since the same inward turn that drains illusion feeds the well: images, music, prayer, and sleep all run closer to the surface. Escapism deserves watching during this stretch, because the urge to blur what is becoming clear rises exactly when clarity approaches. You move with this season by letting the disillusion do its slow work. Whatever is real in your longings will still be standing when Neptune moves forward again.

After its long annual retrograde, roughly five months of backward drift, Neptune pauses this week and turns forward. The station is subtle, shared by the whole world at once and personal mostly where it touches your chart, but the current underneath changes direction. Neptune moving forward carries imagination and longing back out into life. Through the backward months your dream life ran inward: illusions thinned, ideals got quietly tested, and whatever enchantment survived did so on merit. Now the surviving dreams look for form. The weeks after this turn often bring a return of inspiration that wants to be made rather than merely felt: the project resumed, the practice restarted, the vision finally described out loud to another person. Compassion tends to flow outward again too, toward causes and people rather than around the inside of your own ache. There is a soft hazard at the turn itself, since a stationing Neptune can briefly thicken the very fog it is about to lift; confusion, vagueness, or a wave of yearning near the station is common and passes. The reliable gift is orientation. Having spent months learning which of your hopes were mirage, you get a season for following the ones that were water. Idealism with its eyes open is rare, and this is the turn that trains it.

Pluto barely moves at the best of times, and this week it stops altogether before beginning its annual backward stretch of five to six months. A turn this slow and this widely shared works underground; you notice it most when Pluto sits near something tender in your own chart, and otherwise as a shift in the depths. Pluto concerns power and transformation: what controls you, what you control, what is ending, what refuses to die quietly. Its retrograde station turns the excavation inward. The months ahead favor a private reckoning with the buried layer: compulsions that steer you from below, old survival strategies that outlived the danger, resentments and attachments held so long they feel like anatomy. Material that surfaces during this stretch tends to arrive through dreams, moods, obsessions, and the odd disproportionate reaction that tells you the trigger is old. Power struggles in the outer world often lose urgency now while the inner one clarifies, because the real opponent during a backward Pluto is usually a former version of yourself. This is slow, composting work, rarely visible from outside. What it offers you is leverage. A pattern seen at its root can finally be released at the root, and the endings this review prepares tend to be cleaner for the preparation.

The deepest and slowest of the planets resumes forward motion this week, ending a backward stretch of about half a year. Pluto's stations are collective weather, shared by everyone and sharpest where they touch your chart, but the change in current is real: what the long retrograde composted now begins to surface. Pluto moving forward externalizes transformation. Inner work done during the backward months, the compulsions faced, the grip loosened, the ending accepted, starts showing up as outer fact. Around this turn, situations that were secretly finished tend to become officially finished, and the door that closes usually confirms a decision some deep part of you already made. Power themes quicken as well. Buried information has a way of coming to light near a Pluto station, in the world's affairs and sometimes in your own, and influence shifts toward whatever was honest enough to survive the review. If the retrograde asked what you are still gripping and why, the direct months ask what you will build with the freed hand. Intensity around the station itself can run high, a feeling of pressure seeking an outlet, and it favors deliberate release over eruption. What this turn marks, at bottom, is permission: the regeneration you have been preparing in private is allowed to begin in public, at Pluto's pace, which is slow, total, and hard to reverse.

Chiron slows and halts this week, opening the backward passage it makes once a year for around five months. Its stations are shared widely and press hardest where they touch your chart, but the theme is intimate wherever it lands, because Chiron marks the old hurt: the place that never healed all the way and taught you something because it did not. When Chiron turns retrograde, that place asks for a visit. The backward months tend to bring the wound's material up for review, gently or not: an insecurity you thought you had outgrown resurfaces in a new costume, an old grief sends a postcard, a familiar shame walks through a door you were sure you had locked. The revisit is not relapse. Healing with Chiron works in spirals, and each pass reaches a layer the last one could not, so what returns comes back precisely because you are finally able to handle it. Tending counts for more than fixing during this stretch. The season favors care in whatever form yours takes: honest conversation, writing it down, letting yourself be seen by someone safe. It also quietly deepens your usefulness, since the understanding gathered in your own sore places is exactly what lets you help someone else with theirs. You move through this turn best by treating the resurfaced ache as a patient, not an intruder. It came back to be tended, and it leaves lighter.

After about five months of backward motion, Chiron stands still this week and turns forward. Like the other slow turns it belongs to everyone at once and lands hardest where it meets your chart, yet its direct station has a distinct feel: the visit to the old wound is ending, and what the visit taught becomes usable. Through the backward months, tender history had a way of resurfacing for another round of tending. Now the spiral turns outward. Understanding that was raw and private begins to steady into something you can stand on and even offer. This is often when the mentoring instinct wakes: the person going through what you once went through appears, and you discover your scar is a map someone else needs. Pain integrated during the retrograde tends to stop announcing itself around now; the trigger fires and, strangely, nothing much happens, which is how healing usually reports success. The forward months favor practicing the new steadiness in real conditions, letting people see the once-hidden place without ceremony, and choosing work and company that treat it kindly. Chiron never promises the wound's disappearance, and honesty about that is part of its medicine. What this turn offers instead is a season where the hurt sits quieter, the lesson sits deeper, and the healer in you gets more room than the patient.
